I352.screening_reason: Outcome is dropout, not mental health

I353.summary_en: Analyses factors affecting university students' mental health during the pandemic and online learning using data collected at the authors' university and clustering algorithms. DBSCAN yields 8 clusters with 2% noise and K-means 3 clusters, without predictive metrics.

I354.screening_reason: Outcome is employment prospects, not mental health
I354.summary_en: Predicts university students' employment prospects from career choice, salary and self-realisation indicators, comparing RF, SVM and GBDT. GBDT shows the best predictive ability.

I355.summary_en: Proposes a tree-based multi-label model (DT, RF, AdaBoost, XGBoost) to predict stress factors in students. Random Forest performs best with 90% accuracy; the abstract does not describe the data.

I356.screening_reason: Population is women experiencing harassment, not students
I356.summary_en: Examines forms of harassment experienced by women and their mental health impact, mentioning machine learning algorithms and a web app. Data, method and results are not described.

I357.screening_reason: Focus is counsellor job management, not mental health
I357.summary_en: Designs a job management system for college counsellors based on GPT-4 fine-tuned on academic records, counselling cases and psychological counselling manuals. It achieves 95.8% semantic matching accuracy and a 42% productivity gain in a trial across three universities.

I358.summary_en: Proposes a federated hybrid CNN-BiLSTM model to analyse university students' engagement and emotional well-being from engagement logs and emotional expressions. It reaches 96.2% accuracy and outperforms centralised RF, SVM and CNN/BiLSTM baselines.

I359.summary_en: Presents a TriBranch CNN framework with PCA to predict college students' stress. The abstract reports that Fully CTBN reaches 93.29% accuracy versus CNN and FCN, without describing the data.

I360.summary_en: Predicts depression level in students in Bangladesh using psychologist-selected factors and eight classifiers. SMO performs best; no metrics or sample size are reported.

I361.screening_reason: Focus is learning analytics; emotions are an input
I361.summary_en: Presents a deep learning architecture for a digital humanities laboratory that captures multimodal data and facial expressions to classify student emotions. It is a preliminary experiment without performance metrics.

I362.summary_en: Models financial stress in 2,902 college students and its link to academic success using daily activities and wrist-sensor pulse data with J48, RF, Naive Bayes and KNN. The model reaches 85% training and 82% test accuracy.

I363.summary_en: Detects depression among teachers and students of Metropolitan University (Sylhet) from 516 survey responses using logistic regression, decision trees and Gradient Boosting. It reports that causes of depression differ by sex, without performance metrics.

I364.summary_en: Predicts student well-being from personal attributes, academic performance and economic indicators with models ranging from logistic regression to ensembles. Tuned Gradient Boosting reaches 77.63% accuracy and Random Forest 77.29%.

I365.summary_en: Reviews machine learning studies on student mental health and federated learning applications in mental health. It proposes a research roadmap for privacy-preserving federated learning in educational settings.

I366.screening_reason: Focus is engagement, retention and cognitive load; mental health only an indicator
I366.summary_en: Proposes a business intelligence framework combining attendance, performance, mental health indicators, demographics and feedback to monitor engagement and retention, plus cognitive load analysis. No quantitative metrics are reported.

I367.summary_en: Presents EmbraceEase, a web-based mental wellness chatbot that categorises users and generates personalised questions with AI and NLP to estimate illness level and suggest remedies. No data or evaluation are described.

I368.screening_reason: Outcome is academic performance, not mental health
I368.summary_en: Predicts students' GPA in external exams from internal scores, previous semester scores and attendance using several machine learning algorithms. No metrics are reported.

I369.summary_en: Reviews research on difficulties faced by international students in the US and the effectiveness of AI-based chatbots for mental health support. The review method and findings are not detailed.

I370.summary_en: Proposes an interpretable depression prediction model for college students using machine learning with SHAP and LIME on conduct, school functioning and lifestyle variables. It claims accurate prediction without reporting metrics or data.

I371.summary_en: Implements an AI-based data analysis system to visualise university students' psychological test results and support psychologists' diagnosis. It reports faster and better-quality care without metrics.

I372.screening_reason: Population not specified as students; evaluates technology acceptance
I372.summary_en: Develops a mobile emotion healthcare system using machine learning and sentiment analysis and evaluates intention to use with HBM and TAM. Health consciousness, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and attitude significantly affect intention to use.

I373.summary_en: Identifies drivers of anxiety in university students in a non-pandemic period using descriptive analysis and an XGBoost classifier on 194 features interpreted with SHAP. Academic impairment is the strongest predictor, followed by perceived need for help and racial trauma.

I374.summary_en: Addresses the impact of COVID-19 on students' mental health through a binary classification model with neural networks for psychiatric disorders. Data and results are not described.

I375.summary_en: Classifies stress (low, moderate, high) in school children using 980 records from the Student Stress Survey Questionnaire, comparing RF, DT, SVM, KNN and Gradient Boosting. SVM and RF achieve the highest accuracy.

I376.screening_reason: Focus is cross-cultural adaptation and classroom grouping
I376.summary_en: Groups international students in China with K-means based on cultural novelty and psychological capital to build a cross-cultural adaptation model. No data or metrics are reported.

I377.summary_en: Builds a Bi-LSTM model for early detection of anxiety and depression in undergraduate students in Oman using survey data with demographics, academic indicators and HADS responses. The pipeline is described without performance metrics.

I378.summary_en: Proposes ZJ-EduFormer, a Transformer model to predict stress in 2,000 supply chain management students from lifestyle features. It outperforms classical and deep baselines with R2 0.856 and a 26.1% RMSE reduction.

I379.summary_en: Presents a mental health platform for grade 11-12 students with emotion detection, GAD-7, SRQ-20 and PHQ-9 assessments, a chatbot and career guidance. No quantitative evaluation is reported.

I380.summary_en: Adapts the SSI-SM inventory for college students and predicts stress with normalisation, LDA and information-gain feature selection and an MLP. The MLP outperforms CNN and RNN, without numeric metrics.

I381.summary_en: Develops a multi-task XGBoost framework predicting depression severity and perceived stress from university students' daily behavioural indicators, with cross-regional SHAP analyses. It outperforms logistic regression and Random Forest and reveals context-dependent behavioural patterns.

I382.summary_en: Proposes a health recommender system predicting drug addiction risk in students with AutoML (TPOT) and multi-objective feature selection (MOHHO). It outperforms RFE, mutual information and correlation-based selection, without reporting metrics or data.

I383.summary_en: Systematic review (PRISMA, 2015-2025) of voice-based machine learning models for depression prediction in medical students. SVM, RF and CNN are most common and MFCC and prosodic features are relevant, but dataset heterogeneity limits generalisability.

I384.summary_en: Proposes AnxPred, a hybrid CNN-SVM model predicting anxiety (GAD-7) from 2,028 responses across 15 universities in Bangladesh. It achieves F1 99.134%, outperforming conventional models, and LIME shows it captures relevant academic stressors.

I385.screening_reason: Not about mental health; Japanese grammar teaching
I385.summary_en: Discusses the application of big data to college Japanese grammar teaching. No data, method or results are described.

I386.summary_en: Evaluates a Fitbit dataset for stress screening in college students using machine learning. Physiological data such as calories burned and sleep support screening with F1 up to 0.81.

I387.summary_en: Compares RF, SVM and LSTM to predict anxiety disorders (HARS) in 151 final-year students with SMOTE. Random Forest performs best (accuracy 0.9032; ROC-AUC 0.9976).

I388.summary_en: Develops a mobile app monitoring medical students' stress from Empatica E4 physiological data with standard and balanced Random Forest. They reach 91.18% and 88.57% accuracy; the system was trialled with two students during clinical shifts.

I389.summary_en: Predicts mental health status of 79 university students in Bangladesh from smartphone sensor data (GPS, power state, Bluetooth, accelerometer) collected with Beiwe, using three regressors. Random Forest performs best (RMSE 1.303; R2 0.425), with modest accuracy.

I390.summary_en: Proposes a context-aware framework to classify student stress on two survey-based datasets using feature selection, PCA, six base classifiers and ensemble strategies. It achieves 93.09% with weighted voting (Student Stress Factors) and 99.53% with stacking (Stress and Well-being).

I391.summary_en: Classifies depression severity in higher education students from PHQ-9 responses and descriptive text using DNN, LSTM and hybrid models. LSTM achieves the highest precision (90%).

I392.summary_en: Presents Helm, a platform to mitigate college students' digital burnout that combines daily journaling and mobile interaction data with sentiment analysis to measure stress and anxiety. No evaluation is reported.

I393.summary_en: Builds a dataset of 3,701 video clips from 106 high school students in online classes and proposes a graph-based method with attention modules integrating course, event, academic and mental health information to assess state anxiety. It obtains MSE 0.1380 and MAE 0.2768.

I394.summary_en: Proposes a system combining portable EEG and questionnaires to classify the mental health of youths aged 16-25 as good or needing consultation, aimed at institutional monitoring of students. No results are reported.

I395.summary_en: Evaluates a reduced 7-item DASS-21 among KIIT University students with MentalBERT, Random Forest and logistic regression under stratified cross-validation. Classification with the 7 items matches or exceeds the full DASS-21.

I396.summary_en: Simplifies screening scales (SBQ-R, PHQ-9, GAD-7, ISI) using data from 32,868 undergraduates at three Chinese universities, applying mRMR feature selection and four algorithms to 2,632 cases. The reduced scales preserve reliability and shorten assessment time.

I397.screening_reason: Incoherent abstract; adolescent population not clearly students
I397.summary_en: Predicts adolescent mental health from personal, academic and text data, comparing structured models (LR, RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) and NLP models. Text-based models outperform structured-data models, without specific metrics.

I398.summary_en: Predicts student depression on a Kaggle dataset of 27,901 records using XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, HGB, RF and voting ensembles with XAI. CatBoost achieves the best AUC-ROC (0.9210).

I399.summary_en: Classifies social media addiction stages (low, moderate, high) in students from demographic and behavioural attributes using LightGBM, J48 and DecisionStump. LightGBM reaches 98% accuracy; female students and those aged 19-21 show higher risk.

I400.summary_en: Compares RF, SVM, neural networks and logistic regression to predict student depression on the Student Depression Dataset (academic, demographic and behavioural data). Random Forest performs best (accuracy 88.4%); GPA, behavioural markers and psychological tests are the main predictors.

I401.screening_reason: Outcome is sleep deprivation, not mental health
I401.summary_en: Detects physiological responses to sleep deprivation in 424 samples from 129 college students using ECG and accelerometry (35 features) and five classifiers. Gradient Boosting performs best with F1 73.09%.

I402.summary_en: Assesses mental health and contributing factors in 158 high school students (10-19 years) during COVID-19 using an online survey, chi-square tests, path analysis and ML classifiers (LR, SVM, NB, AdaBoost, RF). AdaBoost scores highest (86%); online class difficulties, sleep disruption and prolonged device use are major factors.

I403.screening_reason: Outcome is gender bias in teaching evaluations, not student mental health
I403.summary_en: Detects explicit gender bias in 960 Spanish student teaching-evaluation comments from the University of Bio-Bio using SVM, BETO and DistilBERT. BiLSTM-enhanced transformers reach macro F1 99%, above BETO (95%) and SVM (88%).

I404.summary_en: Predicts students' psychological states from physiological (HRV, skin response, brain activity), environmental, behavioural and demographic features using decision tree classifiers selected by IBM Watson. The best model, a Decision Tree, reaches only about 30% accuracy.

I405.summary_en: Compares machine learning models to predict depression in college students, using SMOTEENN balancing and LightGBM feature importance. Boosting algorithms and KNN show high accuracy, without reported metrics or data description.

I406.summary_en: Proposes CareBot, an online chatbot offering counsellor-like support to students with depression, anxiety or stress, based on surveys, data analysis and natural language processing. No evaluation is reported.

I407.summary_en: Benchmarks ML and DL models to measure depression (PHQ-9) with survey data from 15 top-ranked universities, using XAI to assess feature extraction. LSTM, CNN and SVM perform best, and a CNN-SVM hybrid raises accuracy from 0.979 to 0.984.

I408.summary_en: Proposes a traceability framework to capture, analyse and respond to student stress data using machine learning and computer vision, with data from Google Forms and psychologist consultations. No results are reported.

I409.screening_reason: Career mentorship platform; mental health is not the focus
I409.summary_en: Presents Thunai, an AI mentorship platform for career guidance with mentor matching and sentiment analysis. No data or evaluation are reported.

I410.screening_reason: Not about mental health; curriculum design for a sports major
I410.summary_en: Analyses the feasibility of establishing a physical fitness and health management major in universities from the perspective of health big data demand. No analytical results on mental health are described.

I411.screening_reason: Outcome is e-learning continuance intention; well-being is only a predictor
I411.summary_en: Predicts students' continuance intention on an e-learning platform from survey responses of 2,162 students with seven algorithms. Gaussian Naive Bayes performs best (90.5% accuracy) and a well-being indicator is the most influential predictor.

I412.screening_reason: General review of AI in mental illness; not students
I412.summary_en: Reviews how AI supports identification, monitoring and treatment of mental health disorders in clinical practice. The abstract is partly incoherent and not focused on students.

I413.screening_reason: Not about mental health; physical fitness test equipment
I413.summary_en: Describes the design and marketing of infrared ranging equipment for the sit-and-reach test in college students' physical fitness assessment. No mental health analytics are involved.

I414.screening_reason: Population is Bangladeshi women, not students

I415.screening_reason: Incoherent abstract; no analytical method described
I415.summary_en: Discusses a Watson Studio-based teaching platform for machine learning and mental health education, measured with a questionnaire and the SCL-90 in 145 clinical interns. Method and results are not clearly described.

I416.summary_en: Proposes HCRDa, a hybrid collaborative recommendation method with a dual autoencoder, to analyse social media addiction and behaviour in college students after normality testing and feature extraction. It reaches 98.31% accuracy; the data are not described.

I417.screening_reason: Outcome is sleep disorders, not primarily mental health

I418.summary_en: Aims to identify factors (family pressure, exam failure, economic condition, bullying) behind suicidal ideation in university students aged 18-25 using a questionnaire. The machine learning method and results are not described.

I419.screening_reason: Not about mental health; physical education sharing platform
I419.summary_en: Studies the construction of a smart physical education sharing platform using a big data information network. No mental health analytics are involved.

I420.summary_en: Predicts student stress from behavioural, academic and health indicators using CTGAN augmentation, eight ML classifiers and two DL models with SHAP. Random Forest is best (92.27% accuracy); blood pressure, academic performance, sleep quality and peer pressure are key factors.

I421.screening_reason: Population mixes students with workers and other individuals
I421.summary_en: Explores real-time psychological analysis of conversational text with NLP and machine learning for stress prediction in university students, workers and introverted individuals, and depression detection. No data or results are reported.

I422.screening_reason: Focus is classroom attention and teaching rating; emotions are secondary
I422.summary_en: Proposes a webcam-based system using YOLOv5 and CNN to detect student attention, drowsiness and emotions in class and rate staff. No performance metrics are reported.

I423.summary_en: Discusses the prospects of AI (machine learning, NLP, behavioural analytics, chatbots) for diagnosing and treating depression among students, along with ethical concerns. No systematic method or results are reported.

I424.summary_en: Presents an anonymous web tool that screens university students for anxiety and depression with GAD-7 and PHQ-9, categorises severity and provides recommendations; the title indicates Random Forests. No evaluation metrics are reported.

I425.screening_reason: Incoherent abstract; describes server infrastructure, no mental health analytics
I425.summary_en: Describes the server and media cloud architecture of a psychological smart guiding platform for students. It claims effectiveness without describing data, analytics or results.

I427.summary_en: Proposes a psychological health education consultation platform using Apriori association rule mining on real-time psychological data streams. It reports 99.6% accuracy and 98.3% F1, without describing the data.

I428.screening_reason: Population is young innovative talents, not students
I428.summary_en: Uses AI algorithms to study mental health factors in China's young outstanding innovative talents. Depression and anxiety detection rates are 24.5% and 22.4%, with work stressors, fixed mindset and innovation environment as key factors.

I429.summary_en: Presents Tranquil, a mobile app that assesses university students' stress with the PSS via a virtual assistant, classifies severity with ML and recommends AR-based mindfulness activities. Preliminary evaluations suggest improved engagement and emotional regulation, without metrics.

I430.summary_en: Examines mental health symptoms of Sri Lankan undergraduates using active and passive smartphone sensing (sleep inputs, accelerometer, GPS) with a baseline questionnaire as ground truth and correlation analysis. Sleep pattern and location variance are strongly related to mental health symptoms.

I431.summary_en: Builds a fuzzy clustering model and evaluation index system to assess college students' sports and psychological health. No data or quantitative results are reported.

I432.screening_reason: No data analytics or ML; VR in mental health education
I432.summary_en: Discusses virtual reality applications in mental health education and surveys 100 college students about a VR course. 88% of students would take the course.

I433.screening_reason: Outcome is academic performance; mental health only as a feature

I434.screening_reason: General social media users, not students

I435.screening_reason: Outcome is learning performance, not mental health
I435.summary_en: Predicts student learning performance from attendance, homework scores and class participation using XGBoost with grid search. It reaches 92% accuracy; homework grades and class participation are the most important features.

I437.summary_en: Proposes an interpretable hybrid CNN-SVM model predicting stress (PSS-10) in students from 15 top-ranked universities in Bangladesh, validated with XAI. It achieves 97.34% accuracy, outperforming conventional ML and DL models.

I438.summary_en: Proposes emotion classification of student mental health texts with BERT and Multinomial Naive Bayes, combined with Ethereum blockchain for secure peer-to-peer data sharing. It achieves 80% accuracy and 78% F1; the data are not described.

I439.summary_en: Proposes DDNet, a three-stage stacked ensemble (MLP, SGD, CatBoost, LASSO meta-classifier) for depression detection in university students, evaluated on two datasets with SHAP and Monte Carlo Dropout. It reaches 98.98% and 99.16% accuracy.

I440.screening_reason: Not about mental health; AI in physical education teaching
I440.summary_en: Discusses AI technologies and application scenarios in university physical education teaching. No data or mental health analytics are involved.

I443.screening_reason: Not about mental health; physical test measurement methods
I443.summary_en: Compares standing long jump results measured by infrared instrument and manually using paired-sample t-tests. Results differ between methods.

I444.summary_en: Predicts depression from 14 structured questionnaire items in a balanced dataset comparing LR, RF, XGBoost, SVM and ANN. SVM performs best with 99% test accuracy.

I445.summary_en: Classifies multi-level anxiety (GAD-7 groups) in university students from wireless EEG signals with eleven time- and frequency-domain features and a Bagged Trees classifier, testing segment lengths and channel combinations. No metrics are reported in the abstract.

I446.summary_en: Proposes a conceptual multi-layer AI framework using handwriting as a digital biomarker for emotional analysis of higher education students. No empirical validation is reported.

I447.summary_en: Proposes a multi-level XAI framework (SHAP, H-LIME, DiCE) to predict depression risk in 27,901 students from demographic, academic, lifestyle and psychosocial data. Random Forest reaches accuracy 0.839 and ROC-AUC 0.916; suicidal ideation, academic pressure and financial stress are dominant factors.

I448.summary_en: Designs a secondary school psychology course integrating drawing-based psychological tests with computer vision so teachers can evaluate students' mental issues in real time. No data or results are reported.

I449.summary_en: Develops a culturally adapted depression detection system using PHQ-9, APADSM-5 and CESDR scales from 186 Bangladeshi university students, augmented to 537 samples. Neural networks perform best (91% accuracy), followed by Random Forest (89%).

I450.screening_reason: Outcome is academic performance, not mental health
I450.summary_en: Predicts performance levels of 2,500 learners from digital learning behaviour using XGBoost, LightGBM, RF and a soft-voting ensemble with LIME. The ensemble reaches 99.8% accuracy.

I451.summary_en: Classifies student stress levels from psychological and academic features (anxiety, self-esteem, depression, sleep quality) in 1,100 records using PCA, correlation analysis and a Decision Tree. It reaches 90% accuracy; anxiety and self-esteem are the most influential predictors.

I452.summary_en: Classifies student stress levels from PSS and DASS-21 stress questionnaire responses using Naive Bayes and KNN on two datasets. Naive Bayes performs better with 90.0% and 77.08% accuracy.

I453.summary_en: Examines stress in 130 students aged 20-24 in Mysuru using Pearson correlation, t-tests and ANOVA. Stress correlates strongly with emotional drain, avoidance and emotional instability and negatively with post-graduation CGPA (-0.6894).

I454.summary_en: Quantifies exam stress progression from electrodermal activity in the PhysioNet Wearable Exam Stress Dataset using LDA, CART, SVM and KNN on exam segments. SVM is best (75% accuracy); stress peaks at the start and end of exams.

I455.screening_reason: Population is breast cancer patients, not students
I455.summary_en: Predicts mental health status six months after breast cancer diagnosis from clinical, psychological, sociodemographic and lifestyle data using Random Forests. AUC ranges from 0.81 to 0.90; initial anxiety and depression are highly predictive.

I456.summary_en: Predicts stress levels in 1,120 college students from sociodemographic data and DASS-21 stress responses using LR, SVM, RF, Gradient Boosting and voting and stacking ensembles. The optimised stacking model performs best (99% accuracy).

I457.summary_en: Compares RF, Gradient Boosting, AdaBoost and XGBoost for college student depression on two Kaggle datasets with SHAP. AdaBoost performs best (0.85 and 0.98 accuracy); suicidal thoughts are the most dominant factor.

I458.summary_en: Develops Maxx, a chatbot that recognises students' emotional state and mental health issues via DialogFlow NLP and provides guidance. No evaluation is reported.

I459.screening_reason: Focus is behaviour recognition for teaching quality
I459.summary_en: Proposes a multilevel Random Forest with latent growth curve modelling to recognise student behaviour (including confidence, frustration and disengagement) for teaching quality assessment on the OULAD dataset. It reaches 99.97% accuracy.

I460.summary_en: Develops an AI model that predicts student stress from heart rate, blood pressure, sleep time and stress questions and recommends yoga practices. Stress prediction reaches 94.4% and yoga recommendation 97.3% accuracy.

I461.screening_reason: Outcome is abnormal campus behaviour for management, not mental health
I461.summary_en: Proposes spatiotemporal anomaly detection with isolation forest and an intervention mechanism for students' abnormal campus behaviour. Effectiveness is claimed without metrics.

I462.screening_reason: General social media users, not students
I462.summary_en: Detects stress in social media text using keyword-based indicators, TF-IDF vectorisation and a Random Forest classifier. No metrics are reported.

I463.summary_en: Proposes a hybrid ML model combining physiological signals, behavioural metrics and academic records to predict higher education students' stress and its relation to academic performance. It reports accuracy above 96%, without describing the data or models.

I464.summary_en: Analyses social anxiety in high school students at a school in Thanjavur, India, with the SPIN questionnaire using correlation analysis, clustering and machine learning, and proposes VR/AR interventions. Distress increases with social phobia severity; no sample size or metrics are reported.

I465.screening_reason: Outcome is academic performance, not mental health
I465.summary_en: Predicts student academic performance using mRMR feature selection and an A-CNN-BiLSTM model. It reaches 96.57% accuracy, outperforming BiLSTM and CNN.

I466.screening_reason: Data are general X users; students mentioned only as context
I466.summary_en: Compares Naive Bayes and SVM for depression sentiment classification of X (Twitter) posts from a GitHub dataset. SVM reaches 99% accuracy versus 87% for Naive Bayes.

I467.summary_en: Reviews ML-based stress detection methods and demonstrates stress detection in college students from labelled datasets and facial expressions. It reports efficient accuracy without specific metrics.

I468.summary_en: Automates screening of anxiety, depression and burnout in 886 Swiss medical students comparing an ensemble (RF, NB, LightGBM) and a DNN with information-gain feature selection. The DNN performs best (81.4% depression, 76.65% anxiety, 73.59% burnout).
